title: Topic thread: navigability, layered memory and the maintenance skill

sections.name: narrative
sections.label: Narrative
sections.content:
A running thread on how an SRS repository stays findable, and how what it learns is kept, tested and let go. Opened 2026-10-27 from the navigation work on muSrs.

Questions the thread holds open
1. What is the SRS maintenance skill? The skill an agent or person uses to keep a repository navigable and its meaning intact over time.
2. How do we structure repositories so that they are navigable? A few purpose-shaped areas at the root, stable once settled, growing consistently; only significant redesigns come up for PR.
3. How do we build up information in layers? Short-term notes and vignettes become long-term structure only by being actively structured and tested against scenarios.

Positions the owner has taken (see the vignettes in this container)
- Semantic integrity is directly related to navigability: if the information cannot be found, or what was learnt cannot be discovered, SRS is not transferring meaning.
- Meaning has a temporal element: some information is valuable now, some for the long term, and irrelevant data must be removed at the right time.
- Short-term memory (small pieces without full context, including vignettes) becomes long-term memory only through the dream cycle, which reviews it across contexts and tests it against scenarios.
- Affirmation does not fit most of this. Confidence is built by cross-checks, not by affirming a fixed truth; solid ground accumulates as the same scenarios play out.

Related: SP-116, SP-117, SP-118 (suggested problems); srs-rust#1490 (navigation tree); the muSrs worktree branch navigation-structure-2026-10-27.
